content.title: When is the UConn-Michigan national championship game? Here's how to watch
content.text: A new men's college basketball champion is about to be crowned. The March Madness bracket of 68 teams is now down to its final two: No. 1 Michigan and No. 2 UConn. Michigan's journey in the Midwest region saw it take down No. 16 Howard, No. 9 Saint Louis, No. 4 Alabama, No. 6 Tennessee and No. 1 Arizona. The win over the fellow top-ranked Wildcats saw a whopping 91-73 scoreline. UConn's run from the East region involved eliminating No. 15 Furman, No. 7 UCLA, No. 3 Michigan State, No. 1 Duke and No. 3 Illinois. While the Wolverines have essentially breezed through the tournament thus far -- their lowest margin of victory is 13 vs. Alabama -- the Huskies are more battle-tested thanks to their four-point win vs. Michigan State and the thrilling one-point triumph vs. Duke. Will Dusty May's Michigan sustain that momentum or will Dan Hurley's UConn prove resilient once again? Here's what to know about the men's championship game: MORE MARCH MADNESS COVERAGE When is the UConn-Michigan men's NCAA championship game? The two sides will battle on Monday, April 6. What time is the UConn-Michigan men's NCAA championship game? Tip-off time is slated for 8:50 p.m. ET/5:50 p.m. PT. Where is the UConn-Michigan men's NCAA championship game? Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Ind., is the venue for the clash. Where to watch the UConn-Michigan championship game online, on TV The game will be broadcast on TBS and truTV. Streaming will be available on HBO Max. How many men's NCAA Tournament championships does UConn have? The Huskies are six-time D1 NCAA Tournament winners, most recently going back to back in 2023 and 2024. Tarris Reed Jr., Alex Karaban, Braylon Mullins and Silas Demary Jr. will need to be key as guard Solo Ball is pushing to be available, but is a doubt. How many men's NCAA Tournament championships does Michigan have? The Wolverines only won the men's NCAA Tournament once, which transpired in 1989. Michigan is led by star forward Yaxel Lendeborg, a possible top-10 pick in the summer's NBA draft, though he'll be playing through knee and ankle injuries in the hopes of a title. Lendeborg is aided by a supporting cast of Morez Johnson Jr., Aday Mara, Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney, among others. 5:28Richard ‘Rip' Hamilton says UConn can win it all when March Madness tips off Richard 'Rip' Hamilton says the excitement of the NCAA tournament is unlike anything else in basketball and believes UConn has what it takes to win another national championship. The Huskies legend also shared what he believes is the secret behind UConn basketball programs’ long-standing success.
